root_cause.text: The nstree `listns()` permission check in `kernel/nstree.c` was too permissive, allowing a caller with `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` in a user namespace or the current namespace to enumerate namespaces that should be hidden, because it did not centralize visibility policy through `may_see_all_namespaces()` and instead used weaker per-case capability checks.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces the old `may_list_ns()` logic—which granted access based on `kls->userns_capable`, `ns_capable_noaudit(user_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN)`, and `ns_capable_noaudit(to_user_ns(ns), CAP_SYS_ADMIN)` for user namespaces—with a stricter check that returns `may_see_all_namespaces()` after only allowing `kls->user_ns && kls->userns_capable` or `is_current_namespace(ns)`; it also changes `kls->userns_capable = ns_capable_noaudit(kls->user_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN);` to `kls->userns_capable = may_see_all_namespaces();`, matching the commit message that says privileged services should not necessarily see other privileged services’ namespaces.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify and correct namespace listing अनुमति checks by using the current namespace and global visibility policy as the fallback path.
intent_record.what: The `may_list_ns()` inline function was rewritten to remove the previous multi-branch capability checks based on `kls->user_ns`, `ns_owner(ns)`, `ns->ns_type`, and `ns_capable_noaudit(...)`. The new logic now returns true immediately only when `kls->user_ns && kls->userns_capable` is true, otherwise it returns true if `is_current_namespace(ns)` is true, and for all remaining cases it delegates to `may_see_all_namespaces()`.
intent_record.how: This changes namespace listing permission decisions at runtime by simplifying and centralizing the fallback access rule. Instead of separately checking owner/user-namespace capabilities and special-casing user namespaces, the function now allows listing when the caller is capable in the user namespace context, when the target namespace is the current one, or when the broader `may_see_all_namespaces()` policy permits it. This can alter which namespaces are visible to a caller and likely fixes inconsistent or overly permissive/restrictive access behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace the user-namespace CAP_SYS_ADMIN check with the correct all-namespaces visibility check when determining namespace listing permissions.
intent_record.what: In do_listns_userns(), the assignment to kls->userns_capable was changed from ns_capable_noaudit(kls->user_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN) to may_see_all_namespaces().
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now determines whether the caller may see all namespaces using a broader visibility check instead of testing CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability in the target user namespace, which changes the condition used to decide namespace listing access.

Add a new listns() system call that allows userspace to iterate through

Author: Christian Brauner <brauner@kernel.org>
Date:   Wed Oct 29 13:20:32 2025 +0100

    nstree: add listns()
    
    Add a new listns() system call that allows userspace to iterate through
    namespaces in the system. This provides a programmatic interface to
    discover and inspect namespaces, enhancing existing namespace apis.
    
    Currently, there is no direct way for userspace to enumerate namespaces
    in the system. Applications mu
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet contains the permission logic for namespace enumeration in `may_list_ns()`, and it matches the described vulnerable construct. In the global-listing path (`else` branch when `kls->user_ns` is NULL), the code grants access if `ns_capable_noaudit(user_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN)` succeeds, where `user_ns` is derived from the namespace owner or `init_user_ns`: `if (ns_capable_noaudit(user_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN)) return true;`. It then also allows access via weaker per-namespace checks: `if (is_current_namespace(ns)) return true;` and, for user namespaces only, `if (ns_capable_noaudit(to_user_ns(ns), CAP_SYS_ADMIN)) return true;`. This is exactly the permissive, decentralized visibility policy described, because it does not centralize the decision through `may_see_all_namespaces()` and instead uses per-case capability checks that can expose namespaces that should remain hidden. There is no sign of the fix in this commit body: no call to `may_see_all_namespaces()`, and no stricter centralized visibility gate before `legitimize_ns()` returns the namespace as listable.
